concepts.label: cbbackupmgr remove sub-command
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the per-sub-command concept this page is about, distinct from the whole tool:cbbackupmgr

concepts.label: Safe remove check
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the default-on dependency check this page describes that refuses a delete which would break a later incremental backup's chain

relations.subject: backup:full-backup
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; the actual enforcement is a refusal rather than an automatic cascade (the command declines to delete the full backup unless the dependent incrementals are deleted in the same invocation), which is the closest existing predicate to this dependency shape
relations.evidence: a backup cannot be deleted if an incremental backup depends on it, unless those same incremental backups are being deleted in the same command.

relations.subject: backup:cbbackupmgr-remove-command
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; inverted sense - the check is ON by default and the flag disables rather than enables it, but this is the closest existing predicate for a behavior gated by an explicit boolean flag
relations.evidence: By default, the remove command will not delete backups which would cause dependencies to be broken i.e. a backup cannot be deleted if an incremental backup depends on it, unless those same incremental backups are being deleted in the same command.

notable_absence.finding: Nothing on this page requires or even mentions a confirmation prompt before deletion - the DISCUSSION section states the operation is irreversible ('Data is not recoverable once it has been removed') but every example in EXAMPLES runs remove non-interactively with no confirmation step shown, and no flag on this page (only --disable-safe-remove-check, which weakens a dependency check, not a confirmation) requires the operator to confirm before data is destroyed.

cross_component_finding: This is the destructive-operation warning the round's briefing asked this batch to look for, stated as plainly as any page in the module gets: 'Removing a backup repository will remove data permanently from disk. Data is not recoverable once it has been removed.' The page also documents a real safety mechanism guarding a different, adjacent risk (breaking an incremental chain) via --disable-safe-remove-check, but that check guards against a broken restore chain, not against the deletion itself being unrecoverable - the two risks (broken dependency vs. permanent loss) are distinct and only the first has a safeguard.
